Does this Platy have fish fungus or somethign else?

I bought some Platys yesterday, and noticed this guy today. I isolated him already but I'm still a newbie when it comes to fish and aquariums so I wanted to check and see if I could pin point what it is before trying to treat.

Is tail is a bit nipped or else it's fin rot. Is there white on the fringe of the tail where it's nipped looking? I can't really tell from the top, but are his scales on the white spots pertruding/sticking out?

Is it fuzzy looking? Is it spreading at all? Kinda hard to tell from the top looking-down pictures! It looks like it definitely could be some sorts of fungus, but I'm not 100% on identifying fungus/parasites yet!

Is he eating/swimming around at all or does he seem lethargic? (He looks pretty clamped up from the pictures, but could just be stressed from the move) How big is the container he is in? Does it have any kind of filtration? Try not to feed him too much, it will foul his water quicker.

If you want to be extra sure before returning him back to the tank, I'd suggest getting some API Pimafix (or Malefix, which I've personally used to treat a heavy scale infection in my Oranda, and help some fin damage, I personally love the stuff, I have no experience with Pimafix but I think that's your best bet) and just giving him little doses and see how it develops from there. Bring down his feeding to like one flake a day if he's eating alright and change 30-40% of his water in that container every day before treating him. If it is some sort of fungus, it doesn't look bad at all, and it's definitely a plus that you caught it early!

I'm not familiar with all, or even most, iterations - but it seems like everywhere I turn in contemporary horror lit, there's a Constantine rip-off. I get the fascination, I like the character, but how many authors are going to try to squeeze into that clown car before the audience yawns more than it buys?
I may be off base in my assumption that Constantine popularized the idea of a damaged magician gumshoe (hesitant damned occult hero/anti-hero), but he's the most prominent example I'm aware of.

I wonder what comes next? I'm eager to find out.
Anyone Else Think the John Constantine Formula is Becoming Worn?

The occult detective is an archetype that has roots deep in the genre. John Silence and Carnacki the Ghost Finder were taking down the uncanny nearly a century before John Constantine slipped on that trench coat. Jules Grandin bestrode the pages of Weird Tales like a colossus in over ninety stories, even while masters like Lovecraft and Clark Ashton Smith plied their craft. Constantine's 80s punk rock approach may now be passè, but the underlying occult detective and noir antihero will never go out of style.

I think what's feeling old to me at the moment is the Sandman Slim sunblasted demon noir gangland variations. I sort of had the sense that Hellboy was going to parody the genre, and that when parody of a genre goes mainstream - it loses some steam for a while until it becomes something new… but that doesn't seem to be happening. If anything Hellboy became increasingly serious.

Very grateful for the references to earlier examples - do you think you know who may have been the first (character/author)?

Apparently Fitz James O'Brien had a fella by the name of Harry Escott running around investigating the unknown in stories in the 1850s, though I haven't read any of his stuff. I think part of the problem is that the occult detective has been co-opted by the urban fantasy subgenre which has substantial crossover with the romance markets, so you're going to get a lot of clones of popular series with some bodice-ripping thrown in. The hardboiled detective is a natural fit with horror and California is his native environment, but most of the folks writing the current stuff couldn't hold a candle to Chandler or Hammett.
